title: Dynamic-logo crops across printed materials
slide_intent: Show how variation in crop can keep a series lively while repeated forms and colors help viewers connect its separate pieces.
strategic_value: Swisscom can vary its printed compositions while retaining a common visual family through the red, blue and white surfaces.
demonstration: An oblique photograph shows overlapping printed pieces with different enlargements and crops of the dimensional symbol; small white copy appears on some colored fields.
practical_value: Compare several crops together to see whether variation preserves the recognizable color and surface relationships.

content_islands.name: Printed comparison field
content_islands.spec: Arrange the photographed pieces across the full frame, keeping their overlapping edges and varied orientations.

content_islands.name: Repeated symbol crops
content_islands.spec: Let red, blue and white curved surfaces vary in scale across the pieces so the comparison remains visible.

content_islands.name: Supporting print text
content_islands.spec: Retain the small white text on the lower pieces as evidence of the graphics sharing space with information; do not invent unreadable copy.

ingredient.name: Symbol crop
ingredient.role: Connect differently composed printed pieces through recurring form and color.
ingredient.application: Vary the crop and scale across the printed pieces as shown, allowing some compositions to emphasize a single surface.
ingredient.scope: Observed print examples in this historical case study. No universal crop ratio or type-placement rule is supplied.

reference_purposes.Expression: The print array demonstrates multiple red, blue and white crops from the same dimensional form.
reference_purposes.Application: The photographed printed pieces show the cropped symbol sharing space with small information text.
